answer.rationale: The two degrading metrics this quarter are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so fixing the funnel entry has the best chance of moving both with one slot. Two inherited memories point the same way (memory_86: shorter onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value; memory_31: fewer required signup fields gave a durable SMB activation lift), so I am verifying exactly those two because they are the load-bearing claims for my choice \u2014 verifying the memories that support the plan is more informative than verifying ones I am already discounting. I am deliberately not chasing the competitor with promotional_pricing: memory_73 shows price cuts bought 31% signups and 18% revenue while costing 12 points of early retention, which is the opposite of sustainable qualified revenue, and it is the clearest trap in this memory set. activation_messaging (memory_91) is the strong runner-up and would be my fallback if the archive undercuts the onboarding records. Key risks I am holding open rather than assuming away: (1) memory_31's 'durable' lift is a claim I cannot audit from the summary alone, hence the verification pull; (2) cutting signup fields can raise raw activation while degrading lead qualification and downstream sales-assisted conversion \u2014 memory_44 says enterprise pipeline quality depends on the demo-request path, so a field cut could quietly damage qualified revenue even as the headline metric improves; (3) the current quarter's decline may stem from traffic-mix or competitor-driven cohort shifts rather than funnel friction, in which case a funnel fix will underdeliver. I therefore scope this as a standard experiment on self-serve SMB only, leaving enterprise and demo-request flows untouched, with lead-quality and 30-day retention as guardrail metrics alongside completion, not just top-of-funnel counts.
